ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, EF passes through the intersection point O of the diagonals of rectangle ABCD, and intersects AD and BC at points E and F, respectively. Given that AB = 3 and BC = 4, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given rectangle ABCD, \\
it follows that BO=DO=AO=CO, and AD$\parallel$BC, \\
hence, $\angle$EDO=$\angle$FBO, \\
since also $\angle$EOD=$\angle$FOB, \\
it follows that $\triangle$EDO$\cong$$\triangle$FBO (by ASA), \\
thus, the area of $\triangle$FBO = the area of $\triangle$EDO, \\
hence, the area of the shaded region = S$_{\triangle BOC}$= $\frac{1}{4}$S$_{\text{rectangle }ABCD}$= $\frac{1}{4}\times4\times3=\boxed{3}$.

method.method_draft: Use triangle congruence and area replacement. First read the figure: rectangle ABCD has diagonals AC and BD crossing at O; the slanted segment EF passes through O with E on AD and F on BC; the shaded parts are triangle EOD near the top right and triangle FOC near the bottom right. From the text, use AB = 3 and BC = 4, and that EF passes through the diagonal intersection O. Since diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other, BO = DO. Also AD is parallel to BC, so angle EDO equals angle FBO, and the vertical angles at O give angle EOD equals angle FOB. Thus triangles EDO and FBO are congruent by ASA, so their areas are equal. Replace the shaded triangle EOD by equal-area triangle FBO; then the shaded area equals area(FBO) + area(FOC) = area(BOC). Triangle BOC is one of the four equal-area triangles formed by the diagonals of the rectangle, so its area is one fourth of 3 × 4, giving 3.
